Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple, well-defined pulmonary nodules of varying sizes (some approaching 3 cm) that are predominantly located in the lower lung zones without obvious calcification. This radiographic pattern, combined with the clinical context provided in the question, is most consistent with necrotizing sarcoid granulomatosis, distinguishing it from the upper-zone predominance of TB or the uniform distribution of typical sarcoidosis.
